issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean, but the solution implements addAnimal(Animal) with a void return type. This mismatch between the specified method signature (boolean) and the implemented signature (void) can confuse students about the expected return type and may lead to mismatches with tests or grading expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent. Either update the UML/problem statement to specify void addAnimal(Animal) or change the implementation to boolean addAnimal(Animal) (e.g., return true when the animal is added successfully). Ensure template, problem text/UML, and solution use the same signature.

issues.description: The template Farm.singFarmSongVerse method signature omits the Animal parameter (it is written as singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), whereas the UML and the solution define singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal): void. The template's current signature and partial implementation (which prints parts of the verse but doesn't use an animal) conflicts with the intended structure and may confuse students about the required parameter and usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to include the Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) and adapt the template implementation to delegate line printing to use the provided animal (e.g., animal.getClass().getSimpleName() and animal.messageOnFeed()), matching the UML and solution. Alternatively, adjust the UML/problem text if the parameter-less helper was intended.
